# Glossary and Concept Index {#sec-glossary .unnumbered}

This glossary is the project's alphabetical registry of technical concepts. Each entry gives a concise reminder and links to the chapter or section that first develops the concept; it does not replace the complete definition, derivation, assumptions, or examples in that source. Mathematical symbols and conventions are recorded separately in the [notation registry](notation.qmd).

Add terminology from a chapter only after that chapter has been completed and reviewed. This keeps the glossary a record of established definitions rather than a preview of unfinished material.

## A {.unnumbered}

**Active rigid motion**
: A physical motion that changes a geometric point or rigid body while the reference frame remains fixed. See @sec-planar-rigid-body-motion.

**Adjoint representation**
: The coordinate mapping that converts a twist between body and spatial conventions while accounting for both rotation and the change of reference origin. See @sec-se2-spatial-twist.

**Ament build type**
: The ROS 2 package build integration declared in `package.xml`; common choices are `ament_python` for Python packages and `ament_cmake` for C++ packages. See @sec-ros2-package-development-workflow.

**Angular velocity**
: The instantaneous rate and axis of rotation of a rigid body relative to a reference frame, expressed in declared coordinates and measured in $\mathrm{rad\,s^{-1}}$. See @sec-geometry-coordinate-frames.

**Associativity**
: The property that regrouping operations does not change their result; for matrix multiplication, $(\mathbf A\mathbf B)\mathbf C=\mathbf A(\mathbf B\mathbf C)$. See @sec-linear-algebra-foundations and @sec-se2-planar-rotations.

## B {.unnumbered}

**Basis**
: A linearly independent set of vectors that spans a vector space, so every vector in that space has a unique coordinate expansion in the basis. See @sec-linear-algebra-foundations.

**Big-$O$ notation**
: A bound describing how rapidly a quantity such as numerical error can scale as an argument approaches a limit. See @sec-differential-drive-model.

**Body-to-wheel velocity mapping**
: The inverse differential-drive velocity-kinematics calculation that maps desired body-forward speed and yaw rate to ideal left and right wheel angular speeds. See @sec-wheel-speeds-body-motion.

**Body twist**
: The instantaneous motion of a rigid body relative to the world, with its components expressed along the moving body axes and referenced to the body origin. See @sec-se2-body-twist.

**Build type**
: The declared mechanism that tells ROS 2 and `colcon` how a package is built and installed. See @sec-ros2-package-development-workflow.

## C {.unnumbered}

**Child process**
: A process started by another process; changes made to the child's environment do not propagate back to its parent shell. See @sec-ros2-package-development-workflow.

**Closure**
: The group property that combining any two elements using the group operation produces another element of the same set. See @sec-se2-planar-rotations.

**Colcon**
: A command-line build and test orchestrator that discovers packages in a workspace, orders them by dependencies, and invokes their declared build integrations. See @sec-ros2-package-development-workflow.

**Column space**
: The set of all linear combinations of a matrix's columns; equivalently, the set of outputs reachable through multiplication by that matrix. See @sec-linear-algebra-foundations.

**Commutativity**
: The property that exchanging operand order does not change the result. Matrix multiplication and rigid-transformation composition are generally not commutative. See @sec-linear-algebra-foundations and @sec-se2-noncommutative.

**Conjugation**
: The matrix operation $\mathbf T\mathbf A\mathbf T^{-1}$, used here to change the coordinate convention of a Lie-algebra element or twist matrix. See @sec-se2-spatial-twist.

**Console script**
: An executable wrapper generated from a Python package entry point, allowing a named function to be launched as a command or through `ros2 run`. See @sec-ros2-package-development-workflow.

**Coordinate column**
: An ordered column of scalar components that represents a geometric object relative to a declared basis or coordinate frame. See @sec-linear-algebra-foundations.

**Coordinate frame**
: An origin together with an ordered orthonormal basis used to assign coordinates to points and vectors. See @sec-geometry-coordinate-frames.

**Cross product**
: A three-dimensional vector operation whose output is perpendicular to both inputs, with direction given by the right-hand rule and magnitude equal to the product of their lengths and the sine of their included angle. See @sec-geometry-coordinate-frames.

## D {.unnumbered}

**Determinant**
: A scalar associated with a square matrix whose magnitude gives oriented volume scaling and whose sign records whether orientation is preserved or reversed. See @sec-linear-algebra-foundations.

**Differential-drive robot**
: A wheeled robot whose planar forward and yaw motion are produced by independently driven left and right wheels separated by a track width. See @sec-differential-drive-model.

**Dot product**
: The Euclidean inner product of two coordinate columns, equal to the product of their lengths and the cosine of their included angle. See @sec-linear-algebra-foundations.

**Drift**
: Accumulated estimation error that grows as imperfect incremental measurements are repeatedly integrated without an absolute correction. See @sec-differential-drive-model.

## E {.unnumbered}

**Exact integration**
: A finite-time state update that evaluates the solution of the stated continuous model exactly under its declared assumptions, rather than approximating the trajectory numerically. See @sec-differential-drive-model and @sec-kinematics-integration-implementation.

**Executable**
: An installed program that can be launched directly; in a ROS 2 package, `ros2 run` locates it under the package's runtime layout. See @sec-ros2-package-development-workflow.

## F {.unnumbered}

**Forward differential-drive velocity kinematics**
: Another name for the wheel-to-body velocity mapping; *forward* identifies the direction from wheel velocities to body velocity, not the robot's travel direction. See @sec-wheel-speeds-body-motion.

**Forward Euler method**
: A first-order numerical-integration method that advances the state using the derivative evaluated at the beginning of each time step. See @sec-differential-drive-model.

**Free vector**
: A vector with magnitude and direction but no fixed origin, so a coordinate-frame change rotates its components without adding a translation. See @sec-se2-transforming-point.

**Full column rank**
: The condition $\operatorname{rank}(\mathbf A)=n$ for $\mathbf A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}$, meaning that all columns are linearly independent and the associated mapping is injective. See @sec-linear-algebra-foundations.

## G {.unnumbered}

**Geometric vector**
: A basis-independent quantity with magnitude and direction; a coordinate column is its numerical representation in a chosen basis. See @sec-linear-algebra-foundations.

**Global integration error**
: The accumulated difference between a numerical trajectory and the exact trajectory over a fixed total interval after multiple integration steps. See @sec-differential-drive-model.

**Group**
: A set equipped with an operation satisfying closure, associativity, an identity element, and an inverse for every element. See @sec-se2-planar-rotations.

## H {.unnumbered}

**Handedness**
: The orientation of an ordered coordinate basis; a right-handed frame follows the right-hand rule, whereas a reflection reverses handedness. See @sec-geometry-coordinate-frames.

**Hat operator**
: A mapping from a twist coordinate column to its structured Lie-algebra matrix representation. See @sec-se2-hat-operator.

**Homogeneous coordinate**
: An augmented coordinate column that appends $1$ to a point or $0$ to a free vector so rotation and translation can be represented by one matrix multiplication. See @sec-se2-transforming-point.

**Homogeneous transformation**
: A block matrix combining rotation and translation to map rigid-body point coordinates between frames or to represent an active rigid motion. See @sec-planar-rigid-body-motion.

## I {.unnumbered}

**Identity element**
: A group element that leaves every other element unchanged when combined with it; identity matrices are the identity elements of matrix groups. See @sec-se2-planar-rotations.

**Identity matrix**
: A square matrix with ones on its diagonal and zeros elsewhere that leaves a compatible vector or matrix unchanged under multiplication. See @sec-linear-algebra-foundations.

**Immutable value**
: A software value whose stored fields cannot be changed after construction, helping prevent an operation from silently modifying an input state. See @sec-kinematics-integration-implementation.

**Infinitesimal rigid motion**
: A first-order direction or instantaneous rate from which nearby finite rigid transformations develop; it is not itself a finite transformation. See @sec-se2-hat-operator.

**Injective mapping**
: A one-to-one mapping in which distinct inputs cannot produce the same output; for a matrix map, this is equivalent to a null space containing only the zero vector. See @sec-linear-algebra-foundations.

**Instantaneous centre of curvature**
: The planar point about which a rigid body is rotating at one instant and whose instantaneous linear velocity is zero. See @sec-differential-drive-model.

**Invariant**
: A property that must remain true for every valid input or operation and can therefore be used as a design check or test oracle. See @sec-kinematics-integration-implementation.

**Inverse differential-drive velocity kinematics**
: Another name for the body-to-wheel velocity mapping; *inverse* identifies the reversed input-output mapping, not backward travel. See @sec-wheel-speeds-body-motion.

**Inverse element**
: A group element that reverses another element so their composition gives the identity. See @sec-se2-planar-rotations.

**Inverse matrix**
: For a nonsingular square matrix $\mathbf A$, the matrix $\mathbf A^{-1}$ satisfying $\mathbf A^{-1}\mathbf A=\mathbf A\mathbf A^{-1}=\mathbf I$. See @sec-linear-algebra-foundations.

## K {.unnumbered}

**Kinematics**
: The mathematical description of motion without modelling the forces or torques that cause it. See @sec-differential-drive-model.

## L {.unnumbered}

**Lie algebra**
: The linear space of instantaneous directions of a Lie group at its identity, together with a Lie-bracket operation. See @sec-se2-rotation-derivative-tangent and @sec-se2-hat-operator.

**Lie bracket**
: An operation on Lie-algebra elements; for matrices it is the commutator $[\mathbf A,\mathbf B]=\mathbf A\mathbf B-\mathbf B\mathbf A$. See @sec-se2-rotation-derivative-tangent.

**Lie group**
: A group whose elements vary smoothly and whose composition and inverse operations are differentiable. See @sec-se2-rotation-derivative-tangent.

**Linear combination**
: A sum of vectors multiplied by scalar coefficients. See @sec-linear-algebra-foundations.

**Linear independence**
: The property that a linear combination of vectors equals zero only when every coefficient is zero. See @sec-linear-algebra-foundations.

**Linear map**
: A mapping that preserves vector addition and scalar multiplication and can be represented by a matrix after bases are chosen. See @sec-linear-algebra-foundations.

**Local truncation error**
: The error introduced by one numerical-integration step when that step begins from the exact state. See @sec-differential-drive-model.

## M {.unnumbered}

**Matrix**
: A rectangular array of scalars that represents a linear mapping between coordinate spaces once the input and output bases are fixed. See @sec-linear-algebra-foundations.

**Matrix commutator**
: The difference $\mathbf A\mathbf B-\mathbf B\mathbf A$, which measures the failure of two matrix operations to commute. See @sec-se2-rotation-derivative-tangent.

**Matrix rank**
: The dimension of a matrix's column space, equivalently the number of linearly independent columns. See @sec-linear-algebra-foundations.

**Multilinearity**
: Linearity of a function separately in each of several arguments; the determinant is linear in each column while the others are held fixed. See @sec-linear-algebra-foundations.

## N {.unnumbered}

**No-sideways-motion constraint**
: The ideal differential-drive condition that the axle midpoint has zero instantaneous velocity along the body's lateral axis. See @sec-differential-drive-model.

**Noncommutative operation**
: An operation for which changing operand order can change the result; general matrix multiplication and rigid-motion composition have this property. See @sec-se2-noncommutative.

**Nonsingular matrix**
: A square matrix with an inverse, full rank, and a null space containing only the zero vector. See @sec-linear-algebra-foundations.

**Null space**
: The set of all input vectors mapped to the zero output by a matrix. See @sec-linear-algebra-foundations.

**Nullity**
: The dimension of a matrix's null space. See @sec-linear-algebra-rank-nullity.

**Numerical integration**
: Approximation of a continuous-time state evolution using finite time steps and a finite number of derivative evaluations. See @sec-differential-drive-model.

**Numerically stable formulation**
: An algebraically equivalent computational form chosen to avoid avoidable loss of accuracy, undefined intermediate expressions, or fragile special cases. See @sec-kinematics-integration-implementation.

## O {.unnumbered}

**Orthogonal group**
: The group $O(n)$ of real square matrices satisfying $\mathbf Q^\mathsf T\mathbf Q=\mathbf I_n$. See @sec-linear-algebra-foundations.

**Orthogonal matrix**
: A square matrix whose columns form an orthonormal basis, equivalently $\mathbf Q^\mathsf T\mathbf Q=\mathbf I$. See @sec-linear-algebra-foundations.

**Orthonormal basis**
: A basis whose vectors have unit length and are mutually perpendicular. See @sec-linear-algebra-foundations and @sec-geometry-coordinate-frames.

**Overlay**
: A built workspace whose `install/` tree is added on top of an existing ROS environment so its packages, Python modules, and executables can be discovered. See @sec-ros2-package-development-workflow.

## P {.unnumbered}

**Package manifest**
: The `package.xml` file declaring a ROS 2 package's identity, licence, dependencies, and build type. See @sec-ros2-package-development-workflow.

**Passive coordinate change**
: A change in the coordinate frame used to describe an unchanged geometric object; nothing physically moves. See @sec-planar-rigid-body-motion.

**Planar pose**
: The position and orientation of a planar rigid body relative to a reference frame, commonly represented by two position coordinates and one heading angle. See @sec-differential-drive-model and @sec-planar-rigid-body-motion.

**Planar twist**
: A three-component representation combining two linear-velocity components and one angular-velocity component for an instantaneous planar rigid-body motion. See @sec-se2-hat-operator.

**Pose**
: The position and orientation of a rigid body relative to a chosen reference frame. See @sec-planar-rigid-body-motion.

**Position coordinate**
: The coordinates of a geometric point relative to a frame origin, expressed along that frame's basis axes. See @sec-geometry-coordinate-frames.

**Pure rolling**
: The ideal wheel-ground condition in which wheel rim motion and longitudinal ground displacement agree without slip, giving $v_i=r\dot\phi_i$. See @sec-differential-drive-model.

## R {.unnumbered}

**Radian**
: The dimensionless SI angle measure defined as arc length divided by radius; the label $\mathrm{rad}$ is retained to communicate angular meaning. See @sec-differential-drive-model.

**Rank-nullity theorem**
: For $\mathbf A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}$, the identity $\operatorname{rank}(\mathbf A)+\operatorname{nullity}(\mathbf A)=n$. See @sec-linear-algebra-rank-nullity.

**Relative-position vector**
: A vector directed from one declared point to another, expressed in a declared coordinate frame. See @sec-geometry-coordinate-frames.

**Resource index**
: The installed ament registry that ROS 2 queries to discover package resources and installation prefixes. See @sec-ros2-package-development-workflow.

**Resource marker**
: A file installed in the ament resource index whose filename registers a ROS 2 package. See @sec-ros2-package-development-workflow.

**Rigid-body point-velocity relation**
: The equation stating that a body-fixed point's velocity equals a reference point's translational velocity plus the rotational contribution from angular velocity and relative position. See @sec-geometry-coordinate-frames and @sec-se2-body-point-velocity.

**ROS 2 package**
: A unit combining source code with the metadata required for building, installing, dependency resolution, and discovery by ROS 2 tools. See @sec-ros2-package-development-workflow.

**ROS 2 workspace**
: A directory structure that holds packages developed and built together, conventionally separated into editable source, build state, installed runtime layout, and logs. See @sec-ros2-package-development-workflow.

**Rotation matrix**
: An orthogonal matrix with determinant $+1$ that maps vector coordinates between right-handed orthonormal frames while preserving lengths, angles, and orientation. See @sec-geometry-coordinate-frames.

## S {.unnumbered}

**Scalar multiplication**
: Multiplication of a vector by a real number, scaling its magnitude and reversing its direction when the scalar is negative. See @sec-linear-algebra-foundations.

**Signed turning radius**
: The instantaneous distance from the body origin to the centre of curvature with a sign indicating which side of the robot contains that centre. See @sec-differential-drive-model.

**Singular matrix**
: A square matrix that has no inverse and maps at least one nonzero input direction to zero. See @sec-linear-algebra-foundations.

**Sinc function**
: The unnormalised function $\operatorname{sinc}(z)=\sin z/z$ for $z\ne0$, extended continuously by $\operatorname{sinc}(0)=1$. See @sec-differential-drive-model.

**Skew-symmetric matrix**
: A square matrix satisfying $\mathbf A^\mathsf T=-\mathbf A$; planar angular-velocity matrices have this structure. See @sec-se2-rotation-derivative-tangent.

**Software contract**
: A precise statement of an operation's accepted inputs, returned outputs, assumptions, validation, failure behaviour, and observable side effects. See @sec-kinematics-integration-implementation.

**Source a shell script**
: Execute a script in the current shell so its environment-variable changes persist after the script finishes. See @sec-ros2-package-development-workflow.

**Span**
: The set of every linear combination that can be formed from a given collection of vectors. See @sec-linear-algebra-foundations.

**Spatial twist expressed in the world frame**
: A twist representation whose velocity field is expressed using fixed world coordinates and referenced to the world origin. See @sec-se2-spatial-twist.

**Special Euclidean group $SE(2)$**
: The group of finite planar rigid transformations that combine a rotation in $SO(2)$ with a planar translation. See @sec-planar-rigid-body-motion.

**Special orthogonal group**
: The group $SO(n)$ of orthogonal matrices with determinant $+1$, representing proper rotations in $n$ dimensions. See @sec-linear-algebra-foundations and @sec-se2-planar-rotations.

**Standard basis**
: The coordinate basis whose $i$th vector has entry $1$ in position $i$ and zero in every other position. See @sec-linear-algebra-foundations.

**Symbolic link**
: A filesystem reference that points to another path; `colcon build --symlink-install` uses links for supported files so edits to existing source may appear in the installed layout without copying. See @sec-ros2-package-development-workflow.

## T {.unnumbered}

**Tangent direction**
: The derivative of a differentiable curve through a selected point, equivalently the limiting direction of secant lines approaching that point. See @sec-se2-rotation-derivative-tangent.

**Tangent space**
: The vector space containing all tangent directions of admissible differentiable curves through a selected point of a smooth set. See @sec-se2-rotation-derivative-tangent and @sec-se2-hat-operator.

**Track width**
: The lateral distance between the effective left and right wheel contact lines of a differential-drive robot. See @sec-wheel-speeds-body-motion.

**Transformation composition**
: Combining successive coordinate changes or rigid motions by matrix multiplication; with column vectors, the rightmost transformation acts first. See @sec-planar-rigid-body-motion.

**Translation**
: A displacement that changes point positions without changing vector directions or rigid-body orientation. See @sec-geometry-coordinate-frames and @sec-se2-transforming-point.

**Transpose**
: The operation that exchanges a matrix's rows and columns. See @sec-linear-algebra-foundations.

**Twist**
: A coordinate representation of a rigid body's instantaneous motion combining linear and angular velocity; it is a rate, not a finite pose. See @sec-se2-body-twist.

## U {.unnumbered}

**Underlay**
: An existing sourced ROS installation or workspace on which another workspace depends. See @sec-ros2-package-development-workflow.

**Unit vector**
: A nonzero vector divided by its Euclidean norm so that its resulting norm is one. See @sec-linear-algebra-vector-norm.

## V {.unnumbered}

**Vee operator**
: The inverse of a declared hat operator, recovering a twist coordinate column from its structured Lie-algebra matrix. See @sec-se2-hat-operator.

**Velocity kinematics**
: An algebraic relationship among instantaneous velocities that does not integrate pose or model the forces producing the motion. See @sec-wheel-speeds-body-motion.

## W {.unnumbered}

**Wheel-to-body velocity mapping**
: The differential-drive calculation that maps left and right wheel angular speeds to body-forward speed and yaw rate. See @sec-wheel-speeds-body-motion.

**Workspace**
: See **ROS 2 workspace**.

## Z {.unnumbered}

**Zero-order hold**
: The assumption that an input remains constant throughout one sampling or integration interval. See @sec-differential-drive-model.
